### Nav

Must be clear. No cute names. Often shows solutions by company size and/or persona role. For horizontal products, often shows solutions by industry. 

See this example from Monday:  
![][image1]  
![][image2]![][image3]

### Hero

Describe what the product does in its broadest possible use case, and ideally why it’s better than other offerings, or how it eliminates or mitigates common pain points.

### Social trust

Any of a mix of the following. Typically we want to establish as much trust as possible. Important to note though that these elements must come off as credible in order to be effective. A quote without attribution or a marquee full of logos no one has ever seen before might hurt trust more than help it.

* Recognizable client logos  
* “As seen in” media logos  
* TrustPilot reviews  
* Customer testimonials  
* Success metrics

### Pain point(s)

This section doesn’t always exist, but it can be compelling to reflect back to the buyer an understanding of their pain points. The messaging becomes a story that the buyer can relate to, making them more open to entertaining the product as a solution to those pain points. It’s important to present the product or offering as a solution, rather than just a product with features. We always try to tie the features back to benefits that directly improve the workflows and further the business goals of the buyer and their business.

### About

Often includes success metrics to quantify the value of the product, or an overview of the product’s core features framed as benefits to the buyer.

### Use cases

* Show clients or use cases across industries (if relevant) to communicate that the product works for various industries. If doing this, it’s important not to accidentally make it seem like the product is built for only one of some of its industries  
* And/or: show use cases across teams, workflows, or other relevant categories. The client should have their use cases clearly defined.

### How it Works

Break down the core use case of the product into easy to understand steps. Graphics or product shots often help explain this.

### Secondary features / benefits

Oftentimes a product has additional features that the business wants to make sure buyers are aware of, but not lead with them.

* ![][image4]

### Case study

Quantify the product’s value to a specific customer. Often linking to a blog post about the same.

### Partnerships

Show partner logos or highlight a particular major partnership. For example, HumanFirst highlights their partnership with Google.

### Recent blog posts

Self explanatory

### Newsletter signup

If you plan on sending out newsletters or wants to build up a mailing list

### CTA section

Common CTAs: Book a demo, get in touch, join waitlist
